plants.name: Cosmos bipinnatus
plants.description: Airy, daisy-like blooms float on feathery, thread-fine foliage. They sway in the autumn breeze and draw bees and butterflies to sunny borders and meadow plantings.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late spring to first frost; in mild autumn regions it often continues into late October
plants.location: Gardens in the southern and central United States, Mexico (native range), and mild temperate regions of the Northern Hemisphere
plants.funFact: Cosmos comes from the Greek word for order or harmony. Spanish priests in Mexico are said to have grown the plants in mission gardens.

plants.name: Jacaranda mimosifolia
plants.description: In full bloom, the tree becomes a cloud of lavender-blue trumpets. The flowers carpet streets and lawns in violet when they fall, and the display makes spring in the southern hemisphere unmistakable.
plants.bloomingSeason: Mid-spring, roughly October to November in the Southern Hemisphere
plants.location: Sydney and Brisbane in Australia, Pretoria in South Africa, and Buenos Aires in Argentina
plants.funFact: Pretoria is nicknamed the Jacaranda City because tens of thousands of these trees line its streets. Local lore says a fallen blossom landing on your head brings good luck.

plants.name: Nerine bowdenii
plants.description: When most borders are fading, this bulb sends up bare stems topped with sparkling, ribbon-petaled pink flowers. The petals shimmer as though dusted with glitter.
plants.location: Native to South Africa's Eastern Cape and Drakensberg region. Widely grown in gardens in the UK and temperate Europe.
plants.funFact: The flowers appear before the strap-like leaves, and the plant blooms best when its bulbs are crowded and baked by summer sun.
